Minimum Average Annual Turnover of the Bidder The bidder shall have a minimum average annual turnover of INR 21 Lakh (Rupees Twenty One Lakh only) during the last three financial years.

The bidder shall submit documentary evidence in support of the above require ment, such as: Audited financial statements; Balance sheets; Profit and Loss Statements; and/or A turnover certificate issued by a Chartered Accountant. The submitted documents shall clearly establish compliance with the prescribed minimum average annual turnover requirement. 2. Minimum Average Annual Turnover of the OEM The Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) shall have a minimum average a nnual turnover of INR 1.72 Crore (Rupees One Crore Seventy Two Lakh only) during the last three financial years. The bidder shall submit documentary evidence in support of the OEM's turnover requirement, such as: Audited financial statements; Balance sheets; Profit and Loss Statements; and/or A turnover certificate issued by a Chartered Accountant. The bidder shall be responsible for ensuring that adequate documentary eviden ce of the OEM's financial capability is submitted along with the technical bid. 3. Past Experience The bidder and/or the OEM shall have a minimum of five (5) years of experi ence in the supply, installation, commissioning, operation support, maintenanc e and/or servicing of the same or similar type of equipment. The bidder shall submit documentary evidence demonstrating such experience, including, wherever applicable: Purchase Orders; Supply Orders; Installation and Commissioning Certificates; Performance Certificates; Work Orders; Completion Certificates; and/or Other relevant documentary evidence acceptable to the Purchaser. The Purchaser reserves the right to verify the submitted experience credentials from the concerned end users, institutions, organizations, or other relevant sour ces.

4. Warranty The supplied equipment shall be covered by a comprehensive warranty for a period of five (5) years from the date of successful installation and commis sioning of the complete system. The comprehensive warranty shall cover, without any additional cost to the Purchaser, all items and services necessary to keep the equipment in proper working condition, including but not limited to: All parts and components of the equipment; Computer, control system and associated hardware; Data-acquisition system and associated hardware; Software and software-related functionality supplied with the equipment; Accessories supplied as part of the system; Labour and service charges; Repairs and troubleshooting; Replacement of defective, failed, damaged or non-performing components; and Any other item, component, consumable or service required to maintain th e supplied system in proper working condition during the warranty period, wherever such item is covered under the comprehensive warranty. The bidder/OEM shall ensure timely rectification of defects and replaceme nt of defective or failed components throughout the warranty period. No additional charges shall be payable by the Purchaser for warranty-related re pair, service, labour, replacement or troubleshooting covered under the compre hensive warranty. 5. Mandatory Presentation/Demonstration Before Opening of Financial Bid A presentation and/or demonstration shall be mandatory for all technic ally qualified bidders before opening of the financial bids. Each technically qualified bidder shall give a detailed presentation and/or demo nstration covering, at a minimum, the following: Technical specifications and compliance with all tender requirements; Working principle and operation of the equipment; Major features and capabilities of the system; Computer-controlled operation; Data acquisition and data-logging facility; Calibration procedure and measurement accuracy;

Software features and data-analysis capabilities; Installation and commissioning methodology; Training arrangements; After-sales service and technical support; Warranty provisions; and Service-support arrangements. The presentation/demonstration shall be evaluated by the Purchaser/Technic al Evaluation Committee. The bidder shall demonstrate that the offered equipment is capable of meeting the technical and functional requirements specified in the tender. Only those bidders who successfully complete the required presentati on/demonstration and are found technically compliant with the tender requirements shall be considered for opening of their financial bids. The decision of the Purchaser/Technical Evaluation Committee regarding techni cal compliance and satisfactory completion of the presentation/demonstration s hall be final, subject to the provisions of the applicable procurement rules. 6. Training of Technical Personnel at OEM's Factory/Premis es As the Purchaser intends to establish and operate the laboratory in accordance with the requirements of NABL accreditation, the bidder/OEM shall arrange su itable technical training for the technical professionals/operators nominated by the Purchaser at the OEM's own factory/premises or authorized training f acility, as applicable. The training shall be designed to ensure competent operation, measurement, d ata handling, calibration, maintenance and troubleshooting of the supplied equi pment. The training shall cover, at a minimum: Operation and handling of the equipment; Computer-controlled operation; Data acquisition and data logging; Software operation and data analysis; Calibration and measurement procedures; Routine maintenance; Troubleshooting and fault diagnosis; Safety precautions; and Good laboratory and equipment operating practices. Where applicable, the training shall also include aspects relevant to measurem ent traceability, calibration records, data integrity, equipment verifica

tion and proper documentation, so as to support the Purchaser's laboratory quality-management requirements and preparation for NABL accreditation. The bidder shall clearly indicate in the technical bid: Proposed training schedule; Duration of training; Number of personnel to be trained; Training location; Scope and contents of training; Name/designation or qualification of proposed trainers, wherever available; and Whether a training/completion certificate will be provided. The training shall be conducted by suitably qualified and competent perso nnel of the OEM or its duly authorized technical personnel. The bidder/OEM shall bear all costs associated with providing the stipulated trai ning, unless otherwise specified elsewhere in the Tender Document. 7. Earnest Money Deposit (EMD): An amount of Rs. 86,000 (Rupees Eighty Six Thousand only) (refunda ble) in the form of Demand Draft (DD)/ Fixed Deposit Receipt (FDR)/ Banker’s Cheque (BC) paid in favour o f “INDIAN INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY KHARAGPUR”, payable at Kharagpur must be submitted with the bid . An y bid without EMD will summarily be rejected. No interest is payable on EMD. EMD will be refunded to the unsuccessful bidder after finalization of the bidding process stage by stage i.e. Technical evaluation an d Financial evaluation. The EMD of the vendor awarded the contract may be treated as part of security dep osit towards Performance Guarantee. EMD shall be forfeited if the selected vendor after award of the contr act fails to execute the same. Bidders has to upload scanned copy/proof of the Demand Draft (DD)/ Fixed Deposit Receipt (FDR)/ Banker’ s Cheque (BC) along with bid and has to ensure delivery of hardcopy to the buyer at below mentioned addr ess within S days of Bid End date/Bid Opening date. To The Assistant Registrar Stores and Purchase Section Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, Kharagpur – 721302. 8. Payment Terms: i. 90% payment of the total contract shall be made after receipt of stores in good order and co ndition, successful installation and demonstration, thereafter certification of your bill by the c oncerned Head of the Department/ Centers/Schools/Units. ii. Balance 10% payment of the contract value may be released against submission of Perform ance Security to the tune of 3% of the total Contract Value or on completion of warranty perio d.

9. Performance Security: Performance Security may be submitted in the form of Demand Draft/ Fixed D eposit Receipt/ Performance Bank Guarantee (PBG) from any of the commercial banks in India and paid in favour of “INDIAN INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY KHARAGPUR”, payable at Kharagpur to the tune of 3 % of the total contract value. The PBG shall be valid for the period of warranty period plus 60 days. The pe rformance security will be forfeited and credited to the procuring Entity’s account in the event of breach of contract by the contractor. The address for submission of hard copy of the Security Deposit is as follows: To The Assistant Registrar Stores and Purchase Section Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, Kharagpur – 721302. 10. Jurisdiction: All questions, disputes, or differences arising under, out of or in connection with the cont ract, if concluded, shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction at the place from which the acceptance of T ender is issued i.e. Jurisdiction of KOLKATA HIGH COURT. Acceptance to this effect is also necessary at the time of opening of Technical Bid. Important Note: Bidders should submit the following certificates as per Annexures A.
